reasoning: Both are correct and secure. A wins narrowly: its per-player state follows the join/leave lifecycle, it follows the project's conventions, and it adds nothing extra. B's comments are slightly richer, but it adds client-triggerable warn spam and out-of-scope attributes, and its lazy state creation depends on the player.Parent guard.

criteria.note: Both remotes and the PlacedBlocks folder are created; placement goes through PlacementRules.validate and the part comes from BlockTypes.STYLES. The cap, the os.clock cooldown and owner-only removal are in place, and per-player state lives in a single PlayerState record created on PlayerAdded (including existing players) and cleared on PlayerRemoving.
onRemoveBlock checks typeof/IsA('BasePart') and `blockOwners[block] ~= player` before calling Destroy; PlaceBlock arguments are typed unknown and passed to the validator.
The only substantive comment explains why handlers skip players with no state (deferred signals after PlayerRemoving), and `-- seconds` gives the unit of a literal.
Comments are short. The section banners sit at top level, not inside functions, and appear to be the project's header convention, though they add visual bulk.
The description header describes the file as it stands, with no change history.
Reuses BlockTypes.STYLES and PlacementRules.BLOCK_SIZE/validate, has strict types, stays server-only, and passes all checks.
